title: Durable Release Execution Recovery & Unknown-Outcome Safety
blockedOrProviderUnavailable: External production cloud provider reconciliation is unavailable in the test environment; ProviderReconciliationResult is exercised via a deterministic test double that never fabricates DEPLOYED without a durable intent transition.
recoveryGuarantees: An exception escaping the deployment provider returns RECOVERY_REQUIRED, never FAIL and never DEPLOYED. Emits release.execution.provider_unknown audit with the error reason.
The bridge transitions an intent to RECOVERY_REQUIRED when the deployment orchestrator throws, because the intent is already DEPLOYING and the external side effect may have occurred.

ReleaseExecutionProvider gains an optional reconcile() method returning DEPLOYED | NOT_DEPLOYED | UNKNOWN. Providers without reconcile() remain valid; recovery stays RECOVERY_REQUIRED when it is absent.
Same-attempt retry remains authorized; different-attempt reuse is blocked via consumedByAttemptId fencing (unchanged from Phase 138/172).
Intent identity includes attemptId: different attemptId produces a distinct intentKey, so replay is caught at the authorization-consumption layer rather than silently reusing an intent.
Durable lease fencing prevents a stale worker from releasing or renewing a lease it does not own; expired leases can be re-acquired.
Terminal intent transitions (KNOWN_GOOD, FAILED, BLOCKED, RECOVERY_REQUIRED) persist across process restart, including recoveryReason.
dispatch() emits release.recovery.already_succeeded / already_failed audit on terminal-skip. Best-effort: audit failure cannot corrupt the state machine.
The recovery classifier remains unchanged: DEPLOYING -> RECOVERY_REQUIRED (requires Docker inspection), KNOWN_GOOD/FAILED/BLOCKED are terminal, RECOVERY_REQUIRED stays RECOVERY_REQUIRED.
